lines: A module is delivered more than once inside a single page:
libresign-main: 208 B beyond the first copy, generated by vite 197 B, generated by @nextcloud/vite-config 11 B.
libresign-external: 197 B beyond the first copy, generated by vite 197 B.
libresign-settings: 197 B beyond the first copy, generated by vite 197 B.
libresign-validation: 197 B beyond the first copy, generated by vite 197 B.
libresign-init: 12,023 B beyond the first copy, @nextcloud/files 11,058 B, @nextcloud/paths 681 B, @nextcloud/sharing 284 B.
All 6 pages load the same 1 file: 198,563 B raw, 73,954 B gzip, 54.9 % of the smallest page (libresign-tab, 361,740 B).
Inside: @vue/runtime-core 62,639 B, vite-plugin-node-polyfills 29,432 B, @vue/runtime-dom 26,348 B, dompurify 24,422 B, @vue/reactivity 17,736 B.
moment, 292,381 B on the libresign-main page: carries its locale data; luxon and date-fns are a fraction of it.
vite-plugin-node-polyfills, 57,468 B on the libresign-main page: Node APIs polyfilled into a browser bundle.
1,801 B in 3 pieces of 3 files have no owner: no mapping covers them, and the code matches no file of a neighbouring module, of the app, or of the bundler and its plugins.
No package is imported as a whole: every package contributes only the modules that are used (204 packages, 913 modules).
On this measure the form of importing is exhausted. A root import whose barrel the bundler removes completely leaves no trace, so this is evidence, not proof.
No bundler chunk in js and css is left without something that loads it.
